A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP-LLM work and contain the complete main text and Appendices A-E. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original perplexity, downstream-task, latency, memory, and QoS evaluations, including ablations and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The three-stage precision assignment, regularized fine-tuning, quantile thresholds, hybrid estimator, and asynchronous estimation remain unchanged. V2's candidate-precision terminology and fuller Algorithm 1 clarify the existing procedure, including previously implicit list initialization.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText2, C4, GSM8K, MBPP, BBH, MATH-500, and Alpaca. The alternate calibration dataset and appendix decoding examples are also retained; no task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: LLM-MQ and HAWQ-V2 remain the benchmark comparators, and latency comparisons still use LLM-MQ. Exact-estimator comparisons and the FP16/HAWQ-V2 decoding examples are unchanged. The newly named gpt-fast is an implementation foundation, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Model configurations, calibration samples, training hyperparameters, prompting, metrics, precision budgets, hardware, and latency controls remain unchanged across Section 6 and Appendices B-C. Naming gpt-fast supplies implementation provenance consistent with v1's PyTorch/torch.compile description, rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain exact-versus-approximate estimation comparisons, hybrid/asynchronous latency ablations, precision-distribution analyses, the h/l selection study, calibration-set sensitivity, and decoding case studies. Removing the main-text pointer to Appendix C.3 does not remove that ablation.

E5.justification: The ten latency repetitions in Appendix B.1 and the empirical 15% error/91% confidence statement in Section 5.1 are unchanged. Neither version introduces benchmark error bars, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 14 tables retain identical entries and values. For example, Table 1's Llama-3-8B WikiText2 perplexities at a 4-bit target under a 5-bit memory budget remain 6.59 for DP-LLM, 6.83 for HAWQ-V2, and 7.07 for LLM-MQ. Plotted results and Appendix E responses also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1-9, the Johnson-Lindenstrauss reasoning, Taylor/Fisher approximations, and optimization constraints are retained. V2 names the existing R-squared threshold and restates existing precision definitions without changing their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The claims about dynamic layer sensitivity, input-dependent precision assignment, lightweight selection, and superior performance-latency tradeoffs remain intact. V2 emphasizes the already-defined relative-error proxy in the contribution list without substantively expanding the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explicit complexity rationale for restricting candidate sets to two precisions and elaborates the regression/projection cost-versus-applicability tradeoff in Sections 3 and 5.1. Interpretations of benchmark results and Appendix D's decoding-only and best-effort QoS limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project repository pointer, identifies gpt-fast as the inference foundation, and explicitly states that calibration data determine the regression coefficients and R-squared values. Conversely, it replaces v1's explicit gradient-descent description for tuning G with less specific offline-tuning wording. These are documentation changes.

R1.justification: V2 newly credits gpt-fast in Section 6.2 and Appendix B.1. The 40-entry bibliography and broader quantization positioning remain unchanged. New citations there and in Section 2.2 render as unresolved question marks, preventing identification of the intended additional references.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the abstract, locally rewrites introduction and method passages, standardizes 'decoding step,' expands Section 4's title, and adds estimator subheadings and acknowledgments. The overall section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 compacts the author block, updates figure labels and captions, and reformats Algorithm 1. Tables 2, 3, and 6 relocate as the text reflows, and appendix pagination becomes continuous. All 11 figures and 14 tables are retained without substantive graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 offers a modest net improvement through clearer offline/runtime explanations, more explicit pseudocode and estimator-calibration details, and a project repository pointer. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. New unresolved citations and the less specific description of G optimization reduce traceability and temper these documentation gains.
